purpose: Migalastat is used to treat Fabry disease, a rare inherited condition where the body cannot properly break down a fatty substance called globotriaosylceramide (GL-3). This buildup can cause problems with the heart, kidneys, and nervous system. Migalastat is used in adults and teenagers aged 12 and older who have a specific type of gene mutation that makes it suitable for them.
how_it_works: In Fabry disease, a natural enzyme called alpha-galactosidase A is faulty and cannot do its job properly. Migalastat works like a 'helper' that binds to this faulty enzyme and helps it fold into the right shape so it can work better. By stabilizing the enzyme, it helps the body break down the harmful fatty buildup more effectively.
common_side_effects: Headache, nausea, runny or stuffy nose, urinary tract infections, fever, dizziness, stomach pain, diarrhea, and fatigue. Most of these are mild and tend to improve over time.
warnings: This medicine only works for people with certain specific gene mutations — your doctor will do a genetic test first to confirm it is right for you. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it may harm your baby. Use effective birth control during treatment. It is taken on an empty stomach, so avoid food for at least 2 hours before and 2 hours after each dose. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, as some can interact with it.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 123 mg capsule taken by mouth every other day (every 48 hours). It must be taken on an empty stomach — no food 2 hours before or 2 hours after taking it. Try to take it at the same time on your dosing days to keep a consistent routine.
